core_obligations: Set up the transport: for a special cocontinuous functor u : C -> D with associated equivalence of topoi g, put O' = g_*O with identity structure map and F' = g_*F (proof lines 3214-3222).

Reduce each local property P_l to the corresponding global property P_g on the target, using that P_g is already known to be intrinsic, so that it remains to prove the equivalence of P_l(C,O,F) and P_l(D,O',F') (proof lines 3223-3236).
Verify this equivalence for the properties (1)-(7) listed in the definition, one by one, along the body of the proof.

Handle the coherent case at the end: transport a finite presentation through the equivalence Sh(C/U) = Sh(D/u(U)) and conclude that the relevant kernel is of finite type, hence that coherence is intrinsic as well (proof lines 3325-3332).
proof_roadmap: Transport the module and the structure sheaf along the topos equivalence.
Reduce to the already-intrinsic global properties.
Check the equivalence property by property, with coherence last.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that each of the properties (1)-(8) defining the local behaviour of a module on a site is intrinsic, i.e. invariant under the equivalence of topoi induced by a special cocontinuous functor. The proof transports the data along that equivalence: it sets O' = g_*O with the identity structure map and F' = g_*F, and reduces each property P_l to the corresponding global property P_g on the target site, which is already known to be intrinsic, so that only the equivalence P_l(C,O,F) iff P_l(D,O',F') must be checked (proof lines 3214-3236). The bulk of the proof verifies this equivalence property by property, and the coherent case is handled at the end by a finite type argument on a kernel (proof lines 3325-3332). H2: the transport of each local property across the topos equivalence, and the closing finite type argument for coherence, are the substance of a long but written-out verification.
